status_summary: No bill or law codifying a single nationwide detention standard that displaces state rules was found; CRS noted in July 2026 that the pending detention bills it lists would add oversight and inspection requirements rather than uniformity. ICE revised its own standards by executive action: it issued Non-Dedicated Intergovernmental Service Agreement Standards on 2025-03-26 alongside National Detention Standards, Revised 2025, and on 2026-06-15 released further revisions that it said reduce the burden on contractors and move toward U.S. Marshals Service pretrial standards. State laws on detention have been decided case by case: per CRS, appellate courts struck down California's and New Jersey's laws as applied to private facilities and upheld Washington's inspection law and Illinois's contracting ban.

timeline.event: ICE issued its Non-Dedicated Intergovernmental Service Agreement Standards, aligned with the 2025 revision of its National Detention Standards.
ICE released revised detention standards that it said streamline requirements and reduce the burden on detention operators; the date is inferred from a news report of a Monday release.

title: Codify one nationwide detention standard that state rules cannot override
uncertainties: The Mandate item is mostly about CBP's transport, escort, detention and search standards (TEDS) and lower court rulings, with ICE mentioned briefly; CBP's standards were not checked. ICE's standards revisions are agency documents and are scored as a parallel step to the codification the Mandate asks for. The ICE 2025 standards page prints no issue date for the revised standards and does not mention state laws; the 2025-03-26 date is that of the companion non-dedicated standards. The 2026-06-15 release date is inferred from a news report dated 2026-06-16 of a Monday release; the 2026 standards were not opened. CRS LSB11463 (2026-07-29) was read in full by the researcher and re-read in review; it lists the Dignity for Detained Immigrants Act, H.R. 7347, H.R. 7335 and S. 4786 and describes no bill expressly preempting state rules or codifying a national standard, but it is limited to the bills it lists, and congress.gov, which is blocked, was not searched for others. A Federal Register API query for detention standards since 2025-01-20 (review, 2026-10-18) returned one unrelated DHS biometrics rule. Whether ICE now applies one standard to all facility types was not established. Detention of children and the Flores agreement are tracked in c05-22, and tent capacity for ICE in c05-05.
